question: Find the slope of the line perpendicular to y = (1)/(4)x + 7
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The slope of the given line in the form y = mx + c is m = 1/4.

The slope of a perpendicular line is always the negative reciprocal of the original line's slope.

Perpendicular slope = −1 ÷ (1/4) = −4.

**∴ The correct answer is -4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation of the line: y = 1/4x + 7

**Formula Used:**

For two perpendicular lines with slopes m₁ and m₂: m₁ × m₂ = −1

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 
• 
 y = 1/4x + 7
 m₁ = 1/4
 
 
 
• 
 Perpendicular Line
 m₂ = -4
 
 
 

 

**Calculations:**

⇒ The given line is structured in the standard form y = mx + c, where m represents the slope of the line.

⇒ By comparing the equations directly, the slope of the given line (m₁) = 1/4

⇒ Let the slope of the required perpendicular line be defined as m₂.

⇒ Since the properties of perpendicular lines state that their product is −1, we have m₁ × m₂ = −1

⇒ (1/4) × m₂ = −1

⇒ m₂ = −1 × 4

⇒ m₂ = −4

**∴ The correct answer is -4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slope-Intercept Form

The equation of a straight line is typically expressed as y = mx + c, where m is the slope defining the steepness and c is the y-intercept.

Parallel Lines

If two straight lines are distinctly parallel to each other, their slopes will always be exactly equal (m₁ = m₂).

Perpendicular Lines

When two non-vertical straight lines intersect perfectly at a right angle, the resulting product of their slopes evaluates to −1 (m₁ × m₂ = −1).
